title: P.L. 119-21 Retains Lawful Permanent Residents on SNAP Eligibility List
description_short: The 2025 law’s SNAP eligibility list expressly includes lawful permanent residents.
description_medium: Public Law 119-21, approved July 4, 2025, rewrote SNAP’s noncitizen eligibility subsection. Its list expressly includes lawful permanent residents, so the claim that the law eliminated SNAP eligibility for green-card holders generally is inaccurate. The accessed statutory text does not establish the number affected or verify the supplied note about the existing five-year bar.
description_long: On July 4, 2025, Public Law 119-21 amended section 6(f) of the Food and Nutrition Act of 2008, SNAP’s eligibility provision. The amendment lists who may qualify: U.S. citizens or nationals; lawful permanent residents; people granted Cuban and Haitian entrant status; and people lawfully residing under a Compact of Free Association. It also says an individual must be a U.S. resident and a household must otherwise qualify under section 6. Because lawful permanent residents appear expressly in the enacted list, the claim that the law eliminated SNAP eligibility for green-card holders generally is inaccurate. The text does not establish how many people lost eligibility or the effects on food access, and this card makes no numerical impact claim. The supplied research note says a prior five-year bar continues to apply to some lawful permanent residents, but I did not verify that detail in the text accessed here, so it is excluded from the asserted description. The source resolves the title’s blanket statement; it does not by itself establish every category that lost eligibility compared with prior law.

source_fact_map.fact: The Public Law was approved on July 4, 2025.
Section 10108 addresses alien SNAP eligibility and amends Food and Nutrition Act section 6(f).
source_fact_map.source_excerpt:
SEC. 10108. ALIEN SNAP ELIGIBILITY.

    Section 6(f) of the Food and Nutrition Act of 2008 (7 U.S.C. 
2015(f)) is amended to read as follows:
    ``(f) No individual who is a member of a household otherwise 
eligible to participate in the supplemental nutrition assistance program 
under this section shall be eligible to participate in the supplemental 
nutrition assistance program as a member of that or any other household 
unless he or she is--
            ``(1) a resident of the United States; and
            ``(2) either--
                    ``(A) a citizen or national of the United States;
                    ``(B) an alien lawfully admitted for permanent 
                residence as an immigrant as defined by sections 
                101(a)(15) and 101(a)(20) of the Immigration and 
                Nationality Act, excluding, among others, alien 
                visitors, tourists, diplomats, and students who enter 
                the United States temporarily with no intention of 
                abandoning their residence in a foreign country;
                    ``(C) an alien who has been granted the status of 
                Cuban and Haitian entrant, as defined in section 501(e) 
                of the Refugee Education Assistance Act of 1980 (Public 
                Law 96-422); or
                    ``(D) an individual who lawfully resides in the 
                United States in accordance with a Compact of Free 
                Association referred to in section 402(b)(2)(G) of the 
                Personal Responsibility and Work Opportunity 
                Reconciliation Act of 1996.
        The income (less, at State option, a pro rata share) and 
        financial resources of the individual rendered ineligible to 
        participate in the supplemental nutrition assistance program 
        under this subsection shall be considered in determining the 
        eligibility and the value of the allotment of the household of 
        which such individual is a member.''.
